record.paper_title: Open Problems on Ultrafilters and Some Connections to the Continuum
record.context_brief: Internal maps versus order-preserving internal maps
record.original_question: Let D be a regular ultrafilter on I with |I| ≥ λ, and let N = ω^I/D. Suppose D admits internal maps between sets of size λ, meaning that for any two λ-indexed sequences of distinct elements of N there is an internal bijection h:N → N sending the ith element of the first sequence to the ith element of the second sequence for every i < λ. Must it follow that for any two strictly increasing λ-indexed sequences in N, there is an internal order-preserving partial function h, with domain and range contained in N, sending each element of the first sequence to the corresponding element of the second sequence?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\lambda$ be an infinite cardinal and let $I$ be an index set with $|I|\ge \lambda$. Let $D$ be a regular ultrafilter on $I$ (i.e., there exists a family $\{X_i : i \in I\}\subseteq D$ such that every element of $I$ belongs to only finitely many $X_i$). Form the ultrapower $N = \omega^I / D$ of the natural numbers (with its standard order) modulo $D$. By an internal function (resp. internal partial function) on $N$ we mean an element of $\omega^{\omega \cdot I}/D$ (resp.\ a function whose graph is the image, under the quotient map, of an $I$-indexed sequence of partial functions $\omega\to\omega$); equivalently an internal partial function is a partial function $N\to N$ coded by an element of the ultrapower.

Say that $D$ admits internal maps between sets of size $\lambda$ if for any two $\lambda$-indexed sequences $\langle a_\alpha:\alpha<\lambda\rangle$ and $\langle b_\alpha:\alpha<\lambda\rangle$ of pairwise distinct elements of $N$, there exists an internal bijection $h:N\to N$ such that $h(a_\alpha)=b_\alpha$ for every $\alpha<\lambda$.

Assume that $D$ admits internal maps between sets of size $\lambda$ in this sense. Must it then be the case that for any two strictly increasing $\lambda$-indexed sequences $\langle a_\alpha:\alpha<\lambda\rangle$ and $\langle b_\alpha:\alpha<\lambda\rangle$ in $N$ (i.e.\ $\alpha<\beta<\lambda \Rightarrow a_\alpha < a_\beta$ and $b_\alpha < b_\beta$ in $N$), there exists an internal order-preserving partial function $h$, with $\mathrm{dom}(h),\mathrm{ran}(h)\subseteq N$, such that $h(a_\alpha)=b_\alpha$ for every $\alpha<\lambda$?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search for this problem on internal versus order-preserving internal maps for regular ultrafilters did not turn up any published resolution. Related work by Malliaris and Shelah on cofinality spectrum theorems and ultrafilter construction is available, but none of the search results explicitly resolve the implication asked here, so the status appears unverified.

status_evidence.title: On ultrafilter construction (Malliaris)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent paper on ultrafilter construction discussing regular ultrafilters; does not appear to settle the specific implication about internal vs. order-preserving internal maps.
status_evidence.claim: No explicit resolution of the problem is announced.

status_evidence.title: Cofinality spectrum theorems in model theory, set theory and general topology
status_evidence.snippet: Develops cofinality spectrum framework relevant to internal maps in regular ultrapowers, but does not resolve the precise question of whether admitting internal maps between sets of size lambda implies the existence of order-preserving internal partial maps.
status_evidence.claim: Related framework but no resolution found.
